purpose: Resolve the Ukraine battlefield-feedback, Palantir data-infrastructure, third-party onboarding, allied production, procurement, interoperability, standards, and replication fog. The wave establishes several exact two-sided institutional transfers while preserving the missing Palantir-specific Ukraine-to-NGC2 or Ukraine-to-allied transfer object.

method.null_hypothesis: publicly governed wartime innovation, allied industrial cooperation, and competitive procurement can generate feedback, replication, and standards diffusion without a single private common design
method.promotion_rule: A transfer may be supported only when the sending record, receiving record, object or method, transfer mechanism, date, and changed implementation are named. Palantir participation in a Ukrainian data platform does not make Palantir the transfer mechanism for every later allied production, procurement, or standards action.
method.combat_rule: Official battlefield claims support the institutional process and reported operational state at their source-defined scope. They do not independently validate every performance number, target, or causal attribution.

records.proposition: Palantir supplies software infrastructure for a Ukrainian government platform that makes structured real-world combat data available to defense companies for military AI training, testing, and validation.

sources.title: Ministry of Defence launches Brave1 Dataroom, a secure environment for training military AI solutions

records.observation: Ukraine's Ministry of Defence states that Brave1 Dataroom was launched with the Ministry of Digital Transformation, Armed Forces, a military-intelligence research institute, and Palantir; was built on Palantir software; contains structured visual and thermal datasets collected from service members; and enables Ukrainian defense developers to train, test, and validate AI models for aerial-target detection, classification, and autonomous interception.
supports: a bounded Palantir role in Ukraine's combat-data and defense-innovation infrastructure
T4 public-private technical integration in one named platform
T6 operational data entering model training and validation
O7 compute and models, O11 public gates, and O13 theater functions
does_not_support: Palantir ownership of the combat data
Palantir control of participating companies or model decisions
a transfer into NGC2, the UK, Poland, or NATO
combat effectiveness of every trained model
system-wide common design
records.next_decisive_acquisition: Acquire the platform contract, architecture, data ownership and license terms, access controls, dataset provenance, annotation, model and user logs, Palantir and Government responsibilities, developer agreements, security review, performance validation, and exit or migration rights.
records.falsifier: Operative records show Palantir did not supply the described platform function, combat data were not materially used, or participating developers could not train or validate models as stated.

records.proposition: Brave1 Dataroom reproduces a public defense-innovation ecosystem by onboarding many companies into a common combat-data and validation environment.

sources.title: Over 100 Ukrainian companies are already leveraging Brave1 Dataroom to train AI models

records.observation: Ukraine's Ministry of Defence reports that more than 100 Ukrainian companies had gained access to Brave1 Dataroom, using structured real-world visual and thermal data to train, validate, and fine-tune military AI models. The platform was created through a joint public-institution and Palantir effort and uses security-compliance gates for developer access.
supports: T5 institutional reproduction at a bounded public-platform level
third-party onboarding and common validation infrastructure
a mechanism through which the state can create and scale a developer ecosystem around operational needs
does_not_support: private-network selection or control of the participating companies
complete applicant, rejected, inactive, failed, or exited denominators
commercial success or battlefield effectiveness
Palantir equity, governance, or residual rights in participants
records.next_decisive_acquisition: Freeze the applicant, eligible, approved, rejected, suspended, exited, successful, failed, funded, procured, and deployed company denominator; acquire selection, security, data-access, IP, performance, financing, and governance records.
records.falsifier: The platform did not materially expand or reproduce a developer ecosystem, access was nominal, or company formation and scaling occurred independently of the platform.

records.proposition: Ukraine and the United Kingdom established an explicit transfer mechanism that routes Ukrainian frontline technology datasets into UK defense production and scaling.

sources.title: Front line drone technology to fuel UK-Ukraine partnership

records.observation: The UK Government states that the two countries agreed to share battlefield technology and that technology datasets from Ukraine's front line would be plugged into UK production lines so British firms could design and build equipment at scale.
supports: an exact two-sided H5 theater-transfer mechanism
a transferred object: frontline technology datasets
a receiving implementation: UK design and production

does_not_support: Palantir as the dataset or transfer platform

records.falsifier: The datasets were not transferred, did not enter UK production decisions, or no product, process, procurement, or scaling change resulted.

records.proposition: The UK-Latvia Drone Capability Coalition explicitly linked positive operational feedback from Ukraine to larger follow-on procurement orders.

sources.title: UK and Latvia launch industry competition to provide thousands of drones for Ukraine

records.observation: The UK Government states that coalition members opened a multinational industry competition to supply FPV drones to Ukraine and intended to place larger follow-on orders upon receipt of positive operational feedback, with additional competitions expected to incorporate lessons from the first round.

records.observation: Ukraine's Ministry of Defence states that the joint working group would exchange operational expertise, develop and test UAS and counter-UAS employment methods, integrate innovative technologies, strengthen interoperability, and ensure compatibility with NATO standards.

records.observation: Ukraine's Ministry of Defence states that NATO and Brave1 launched a joint counter-UAS grant program in March 2026 focused on scaling already validated Ukrainian solutions to NATO interoperability standards and integrating Ukrainian-developed solutions into the Alliance's architecture.

records.proposition: Ukraine operates a public feedback and market mechanism that connects battlefield performance, unit demand, state funding, marketplace orders, manufacturer feedback, and production scaling.

sources.title: Over 500,000 drones ordered by the military through Brave1 Market using combat points
Mykhailo Fedorov: 240,000 drones ordered by the military through Brave1 Market

records.observation: Ukraine's Ministry of Defence describes a digital e-Points and Brave1 Market cycle in which units earn points through combat activity, select products from a public marketplace, receive equipment rapidly, and supply real-time battlefield-performance information to manufacturers. It reports more than 500,000 drones ordered and more than 800 available products in the later record.

records.observation: The combined records identify real-world combat datasets entering model training, more than 100 companies using a common development environment, frontline datasets entering UK production, operational feedback linked to follow-on orders, method and standards exchange with Poland, scaling of validated solutions toward NATO interoperability, and a public battlefield-feedback marketplace.

records.proposition: The Ukraine feedback and transfer mechanisms establish one founder-controlled network coordinating Palantir, allied governments, defense companies, procurement, standards, and residual rights.
records.observation: Wave 07 establishes a Palantir-backed Ukrainian data platform and multiple public two-sided transfer, procurement, production, interoperability, standards, and marketplace mechanisms. The records distribute authority across Ukrainian ministries, armed forces, research institutions, companies, UK and Polish governments, NATO, coalitions, and competitive suppliers. They do not establish common private governance, ownership, planning, or residual-rights control across those mechanisms.
supports: continued testing of Palantir-specific and recurring private roles within the public transfer architecture
does_not_support: system-wide founder-network common design
private control of allied standards or procurement
one transferred Palantir object across the mechanisms
coercive civilian governance or personal extraction
records.next_decisive_acquisition: Require common governance or planning, repeat private-team design, transaction-specific rights, cross-mechanism software or data continuity, selection influence, public-risk/private-benefit flow, and effective-versus-ineffective counterpower comparisons.
records.falsifier: Complete transfer and procurement records show publicly governed, competitive, multi-actor mechanisms with distinct products and no common private control or residual-rights cycle.
